parameters.name: Business Model
parameters.meaning: How the company makes money. Read "Our Business" in the RHP.
parameters.positive: Simple, scalable, easy to explain in two lines.
parameters.negative: Overly complex, or dependent on one customer or product.

parameters.name: Industry Growth
parameters.meaning: Whether the sector is expanding. See "Industry Overview" in the RHP.
parameters.positive: Sector growing faster than GDP with clear tailwinds.
parameters.negative: Stagnant, cyclical at a peak, or heavily regulated.

parameters.name: Moat (Competitive Advantage)
parameters.meaning: What stops competitors: brand, patents, cost, network. See "Our Strengths" and "Competition".
parameters.positive: A clear, durable edge that peers cannot copy quickly.
parameters.negative: Commodity product with many similar listed peers.

parameters.name: Revenue Growth
parameters.meaning: Sales trend over the last 3 years. See "Restated Financial Information".
parameters.positive: Steady growth each year, not one sudden jump before the IPO.
parameters.negative: Flat, falling, or a single unexplained spike.

parameters.name: Profit Margins
parameters.meaning: EBITDA and PAT margin compared with listed peers. See the KPI table in the RHP.
parameters.positive: Stable or improving, in line with or above peers.
parameters.negative: Shrinking, or far above peers with no explanation.

parameters.name: Debt to Equity (D/E)
parameters.meaning: Borrowings relative to shareholders' funds. See "Capitalisation Statement".
parameters.negative: Above 2, or rising while profits are flat.

parameters.name: Return on Net Worth (RoNW)
parameters.meaning: Profit earned on shareholders' money. See "Basis for Issue Price".
parameters.negative: Below 10%, or erratic year to year.

parameters.name: Cash Flow from Operations
parameters.meaning: Cash the business itself generates. See the cash flow statement.
parameters.positive: Positive and broadly tracking reported profit.
parameters.negative: Negative while the company reports profits.

parameters.name: Use of Funds
parameters.meaning: What the company will do with the money. See "Objects of the Issue".
parameters.positive: Expansion, capacity, or reducing costly debt.

parameters.name: Offer for Sale (OFS)
parameters.meaning: Share of the issue where existing holders sell and the company receives nothing. See "The Offer".
parameters.positive: Mostly fresh issue; promoters keep their stake.
parameters.negative: Largely OFS, with promoters or early investors exiting.

parameters.name: Price to Earnings (P/E)
parameters.meaning: Price paid per rupee of profit, against listed peers. See "Basis for Issue Price".
parameters.positive: At or below the peer average for similar growth.
parameters.negative: Well above peers without stronger growth or margins.

parameters.name: Price to Book (P/B)
parameters.meaning: Price against net assets per share. Most useful for banks and lenders.
parameters.positive: In line with peers of similar return ratios.
parameters.negative: Far above peers with a lower RoNW.

parameters.name: Promoter Holding
parameters.meaning: Promoter stake after the issue. See "Capital Structure".
parameters.positive: Meaningful stake retained after listing, no pledged shares.
parameters.negative: Sharp drop after the issue, or pledged holdings.

parameters.name: Anchor Investors
parameters.meaning: Institutions allotted shares a day before the issue opens. Published on the exchange website.
parameters.positive: Known long-term mutual funds and insurers.
parameters.negative: Unknown names, or a weak anchor book.
